mcq.question: Why does `for (std::size_t i = n - 1; i >= 0; --i)` never terminate?

options.A: `--i` is evaluated before the first iteration
options.B: An unsigned value is always greater than or equal to zero, so the condition is always true
options.C: `std::size_t` is a signed type on 64-bit systems
options.D: The loop body is skipped when `n` is zero

mcq.explanation: When `i` is 0, decrementing it wraps around to the largest `size_t`, and the condition still holds. Writing `for (i = n; i-- > 0;)` tests before decrementing.

mcq.question: In `rank_finishers`, what does `continue` do when a runner has not finished?

options.B: Restarts the loop from the first runner
options.C: Skips the rest of this iteration and moves on to the next runner
options.D: Adds the runner with a time of zero

mcq.explanation: `continue` jumps to the next iteration, while `break` would end the loop. It keeps the 'skip DNFs' rule at the top of the loop body instead of wrapping everything in an if.

bonus.question: Range-based for loops hide the index. When do you still need an index, and what are the alternatives (for example `std::views::enumerate` in C++23)?
Write a failing test for an `average_split_per_checkpoint(runners, checkpoints)` function that averages each checkpoint over finishers only, then implement it with nested loops.
